candidates.title: The potential role of large language models in addressing phenoconversion in pharmacogenomics
candidates.abstract: Pharmacogenomics (PGx) is a cornerstone of precision medicine, enabling individualized drug therapy by identifying genetic factors that influence drug disposition and response. However, genotype-based predictions frequently fail to reflect actual drug-metabolizing capacity because enzyme activity can be modified by non-genetic factors, including concomitant medications, inflammation, organ dysfunction, aging, smoking, pregnancy, and other environmental influences. Phenoconversion can generate substantial discrepancies between genotype-predicted and observed metabolic phenotypes, contributing to adverse drug reactions, therapeutic failure, and reduced clinical utility of pharmacogenomic testing. The identification of phenoconversion remains challenging because the relevant determinants are often dispersed across multiple sources of information, including medication records, laboratory data, diagnostic information, and unstructured clinical notes within electronic health records. Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) offer new opportunities to address this limitation by retrieving, organizing, and contextualizing heterogeneous clinical and pharmacogenomic information. Beyond identifying drug-drug-gene and drug-gene-environment interactions, LLM-enabled systems may support dynamic phenotype assessment by modeling metabolic capacity as a continuously evolving characteristic rather than a static genotype-derived category and by identifying relevant modifiers even for drugs without actionable pharmacogenomic recommendations. This review examines the biological basis and clinical significance of phenoconversion and discusses the potential role of LLMs in bridging the gap between genetic predisposition and real-world drug response. We highlight the emerging concept of dynamic phenotype models that combine genetic, clinical, and environmental determinants of drug metabolism and may support more precise, context-aware pharmacotherapy.

candidates.title: Stakeholder Perspectives on the Revision of the EU Tobacco Products Directive: A Census-Level Thematic Analysis of a Public Consultation using a Large Language Model
candidates.abstract: Abstract Background: The European Commission's 2026 "call for evidence" on revising EU tobacco product and advertising rules drew unprecedented engagement. This study analyzed the attached documents containing the most substantive technical evidence. Methods: A census-level analysis of 682 policy-relevant technical submissions (684 of 693 retrieved; 2 excluded as irrelevant) was performed using large language model (LLM)-based computational content analysis (NVIDIA Nemotron-3-Ultra-550B). A three-stage inductive-deductive pipeline generated a neutral 9-pillar taxonomy and mapped thematic presence and stance on tobacco harm reduction (THR) and regulation across all submissions. Results: Evidence-Based Governance & Scientific Rigor (73.2%) and Harm Reduction & Risk-Proportionate Regulation (65.5%) were the most prevalent pillars, followed by Product Innovation, Characterization & Consumer Information (61.4%) and Market Integrity, Illicit Trade & Enforcement Capacity (60.1%). Nearly half (48.7%) of respondents were pro-THR, 37.1% neutral, and 14.2% anti-THR; 80.4% favored regulatory flexibility versus 15.8% favoring stricter rules. Roughly half of Public Authorities and NGOs were anti-THR, whereas most Consumer Organizations (85.7%), EU/non-EU citizens (66.4-69.4%), Academic/Research Institutions (59.1%), and nearly all scientist/healthcare-professional citizens (90.2%) were pro-THR. Manual validation of LLM-determined THR stance (n=68, 10%) showed excellent accuracy (Cohen's kappa = 0.952; F1: 0.95-1.00). Conclusions: The consultation revealed a predominant call for regulatory flexibility and substantial THR support. This challenges the perceived political consensus for precautionary restriction in the EU, though the sample is not representative of the population or of the full, largely short-form submissions. LLM-driven pipelines can transform policy evaluation, mapping complex stakeholder evidence at scale and ensuring technical expertise is systematically represented in the legislative process.

candidates.title: Integrasi Generative AI dan Large Language Model pada Aplikasi Web untuk Transformasi Sketsa Menjadi Gambar Realistis dan Evaluasi Otomatis
candidates.abstract: Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk merancang dan membangun sebuah aplikasi generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) berbasis web yang mampu mentransformasi sketsa dua dimensi menjadi gambar realistis secara otomatis, serta dilengkapi fitur AI review sebagai media evaluasi dan pembelajaran menggambar sketsa. Penelitian ini mengintegrasikan layanan GenAI berbasis diffusion model untuk proses generasi gambar dengan large language model (LLM) yang menganalisis sketsa, prompt, dan hasil gambar, tanpa melakukan pelatihan atau pengembangan arsitektur model AI baru. Metode penelitian yang digunakan adalah penelitian terapan (applied research) dengan pendekatan rekayasa perangkat lunak model waterfall. Aplikasi dibangun menggunakan Next.js sebagai frontend, FastAPI sebagai backend, PostgreSQL sebagai basis data, MinIO sebagai object storage, serta Docker dan Nginx untuk mendukung deployment berbasis container. Studi ini menggunakan pengujian fungsional dengan metode black box testing teknik equivalence partitioning yang menunjukkan seluruh 44 skenario uji pada sembilan modul sistem berjalan sesuai kebutuhan fungsional dengan tingkat keberhasilan 100%. Evaluasi penerimaan pengguna (User Acceptance Test) terhadap 15 responden menghasilkan skor rata-rata 4,38 dari skala 5 (87,59%) dengan kategori sangat baik, dimana fitur AI review memperoleh nilai tertinggi. Secara praktis, aplikasi ini dapat langsung dimanfaatkan oleh desainer, ilustrator, dan kreator digital untuk mempercepat eksplorasi konsep visual tanpa memerlukan keahlian ilustrasi tingkat lanjut. Secara sosial, aplikasi ini berkontribusi pada demokratisasi proses kreatif dengan meningkatkan aksesibilitas produksi visual bagi masyarakat yang memiliki keterbatasan kemampuan menggambar. Nilai originalitas penelitian ini terletak pada penambahan fitur AI review berbasis LLM sebagai mekanisme evaluasi dan umpan balik otomatis yang belum tersedia pada aplikasi maupun penelitian transformasi sketsa sejenis sebelumnya.

candidates.title: Component-based approach to assessing the applicability of large language models in decision support systems
candidates.abstract: The article proposes a component-based approach to assessing the applicability of large language models in decision support systems. The necessity of multidimensional evaluation is substantiated, and an original methodology for component-based assessment is presented, taking into account both the content of the text and its suitability for specific applied contexts. Unlike existing review scales, the approach suggests the use of operational applicability profiles of the response and a decision-making procedure at the level of a specific output. The components capture verifiable properties of the response and serve as the basis for reproducible metrics and evaluation criteria. The approach is oriented toward typical decision support system tasks and can be applied in both expert and automated scenarios. The methodology can be used to verify generated results and enhance the substantiation of trust in them.

candidates.title: HalluciGuard-eye: knowledge graph-enhanced retrieval-augmented generation for hallucination detection and mitigation in ophthalmic multimodal large language models
candidates.abstract: Background Diabetic retinopathy (DR) is the leading cause of preventable blindness in working-age adults, yet scalable early detection is limited by the unreliability of AI-assisted screening. Multimodal large language models can interpret fundus photographs and support DR grading, but they frequently hallucinate - fabricating lesions or misclassifying referable DR - which directly threatens timely treatment and prevention of vision loss. We developed HalluciGuard-Eye to make AI-assisted DR assessment trustworthy. Methods HalluciGuard-Eye combines knowledge graph-enhanced retrieval-augmented generation with hierarchical hallucination detection. An Ophthalmic Clinical Knowledge Graph containing 47,832 medical entities and 156,294 semantic relationships was constructed from clinical guidelines and published literature. A dual-stream architecture uses a Visual-Semantic Alignment Module to verify cross-modal consistency and a Clinical Factuality Grounding Network to anchor generated content to reranked evidence. The Hierarchical Factuality Score assesses anatomical, pathological, and clinical-recommendation accuracy. The framework was evaluated on four public ophthalmic imaging benchmarks. Results HalluciGuard-Eye reduced hallucination rates by 42.2% compared with state-of-the-art medical multimodal large language models and achieved 91.6% factual accuracy for clinical entity recognition on EyePACS. For diabetic retinopathy grading, sensitivity was 89.6% and specificity was 92.1%, representing improvements of 2.4% and 2.7%, respectively, over MedRAG. In the component ablation, removing knowledge-graph retrieval lowered EyePACS HFS by 9.4 percentage points. Additional analyses yielded 87.6% critical-evidence recall@20, 89.2% lesion-location accuracy, and 88.9% sensitivity in a patient-clustered cohort. Conclusions These results indicate that knowledge-grounded retrieval and hierarchical factuality assessment can reduce hallucinations while preserving diagnostic performance in ophthalmic multimodal language models.

candidates.title: RAG-NIMBF: A Non-Invasive, Modular Benchmarking Framework for Automated RAG Configuration Analysis
candidates.abstract: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) has become the dominant paradigm for grounding the outputs of large language models (LLM) in external knowledge. However, practitioners are faced with a vast configuration space comprising chunking, embedding, retrieval, reranking, prompting and generation models, and there is limited guidance on how these components interact. We present RAG-NIMBF, a modular benchmarking framework that attaches to existing RAG pipelines as a non-invasive evaluation layer. It evaluates the configuration space through controlled ablation with end-to-end experiment tracking. The evaluation combines LLM-based answer quality scores, retrieval correctness measures, and runtime indicators. This study validates the framework across multiple generation models on the SQuAD dataset. This process reveals non-obvious interactions and demonstrates how the experiments are tracked. The findings indicate that the retrieval balance of relevance and diversity substantially enhances the relevance and coverage of retrieved context in comparison to a conventional similarity search, with MMR raising nDCG@5 by +4 to +11 percentage points across the swept models. More detailed prompt instructions meaningfully increase how faithfully generated answers stick to the retrieved evidence, especially for capable and reasoning models (+10 to +13pp on Qwen3.6-27B, GPT-4o-mini and Qwen3.5-think, but negligible on the 20B generator). Overall, RAG-NIMBF transforms the configuration space of RAG into reproducible, comparable experiments. By attaching to existing production pipelines in a non-invasive way, it enables practitioners to systematically evaluate and improve deployed systems without disrupting existing workflows. This replaces ad hoc choices with evidence-based decisions.

candidates.title: Sistem Tanya Jawab Resep Nusantara Berbasis Qwen dan Retrieval-Augmented Generation
candidates.abstract: Pengembangan sistem question answering pada domain resep masakan menghadapi tantangan dalam menghasilkan jawaban yang koheren secara bahasa sekaligus konsisten terhadap bahan, langkah memasak, dan konteks prosedural dokumen sumber. Large Language Model (LLM) seperti Qwen memiliki kemampuan memahami dan menghasilkan teks, namun berpotensi menghasilkan hallucination ketika jawaban tidak didukung informasi relevan. Penelitian ini mengembangkan sistem tanya jawab resep masakan Nusantara berbasis Qwen dan Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) untuk meningkatkan relevansi dan groundedness jawaban terhadap knowledge base resep. Dataset yang digunakan berasal dari Indonesian Food Recipes Dataset, diproses melalui tahap preprocessing, pembentukan data question-answer, fine-tuning model, dan pembangunan sistem retrieval berbasis vector database. Evaluasi dilakukan menggunakan metrik ROUGE, Recall@K, Grounded ROUGE, Grounded Ingredient Coverage, Answered Rate, dan No-answer Rate. Hasil evaluasi menunjukkan bahwa integrasi RAG meningkatkan kualitas dan keterikatan jawaban dibandingkan model tanpa retrieval, dengan performa terbaik diperoleh oleh skenario RAG + Fine-tuned Qwen yang mencapai ROUGE-L sebesar 0.413, Grounded ROUGE-L sebesar 0.926, dan Grounded Ingredient Coverage sebesar 0.967. Mekanisme tambahan yang dikonfigurasi pada sistem, yaitu no-answer filtering dan fallback retrieval, juga membantu menjaga konsistensi jawaban ketika konteks retrieval yang diperoleh kurang relevan. Penelitian ini diharapkan dapat menjadi langkah awal dalam pengembangan sistem question answering domain-spesifik berbasis LLM yang lebih konsisten dan grounded, khususnya pada pengetahuan prosedural seperti resep masakan Nusantara.

candidates.title: Adaptive Stopping of Streamed Reasoning for Language Model Agents
candidates.abstract: Reasoning-enabled language model agents can incur substantial computation before acting, although the reasoning needed varies across decisions. Existing stopping signals, such as confidence and intermediate-answer stability, can vary in effectiveness across reasoning models; signals obtained from hidden states or token probabilities also require internal access that may be unavailable or impractical. We introduce StreamStop, which learns model-specific stopping policies offline from prefix-level action agreement. A frozen prefix reader encodes available reasoning text for a lightweight stop head, allowing stopping without access to the reasoning model's internal signals. We construct and publicly release a dataset of agent reasoning trajectories with prefix-level action annotations. These annotations compare each prefix action with the full-reasoning reference action, enabling offline comparison of stopping rules and exact expected-return optimization of a discounted action-agreement objective. Conditioning the head on the discount factor allows the agreement-token trade-off to be adjusted at inference without retraining. In closed-loop evaluations on WebShop and ScienceWorld, StreamStop achieves higher observed success than most validation-selected fixed-budget settings while using fewer reasoning tokens than Full thinking. On WebShop with Qwen3.8-27B, it uses 42% fewer reasoning tokens per episode with similar observed task success.

candidates.title: Orthogonal Boundary Unlearning for Dual-Use Concepts in Large Language Models
candidates.abstract: Mitigating catastrophic risks from large language models requires excising hazardous operational capabilities, such as cyberwarfare exploitation and pathogen enhancement, without degrading benign scientific utility. In these dual-use domains, legitimate defensive science and malicious attacks share vocabulary, syntax, and internal model representations, causing standard unlearning methods to induce severe collateral damage (concept bleeding). In this work, we present Orthogonal Boundary Unlearning (OBU), a mathematically grounded framework designed to eliminate collateral damage on benign dual-use capabilities. OBU extracts a domain-matched capability subspace from paired calibration queries via singular value decomposition on empirical activation covariances, and restricts parameter updates strictly to the orthogonal null space. This guarantees that benign representations experience zero parameter perturbation along the spanned calibration subspace. We present two complementary realizations of OBU: Projected LoRA, which applies the orthogonal constraint during iterative gradient-based fine-tuning, and Closed-Form Weight Surgery, which directly edits model weights in a single analytical step without training. Across four modern open-weight foundation models (Gemma-3-4B, Qwen3.5-4B, SmolLM3-3B, and Granite-4.2-3B), OBU achieves strong dual-use concept separation, substantially mitigates in-context priming attacks, and demonstrates durable resistance against adversarial relearning without degrading benign domain competence.

candidates.title: Toward AI-Augmented Applied Systems: Emerging AI and LLM Directions Across Trajectory Prediction, Cybersecurity, and Engineering Automation
candidates.abstract: This paper reviews fifteen recent publications (2015-2026) spanning trajectory prediction, cybersecurity and trust management, classical machine learning and algorithmic optimisation, and engineering automation, and asks a forward-looking question: where is artificial intelligence — particularly Large Language Models (LLMs), foundation models, and agentic AI systems — positioned to extend each of these research directions next? For each of four thematic clusters we first summarise the current method documented in the reviewed sources, then discuss a concrete, currently-emerging AI direction grounded in recent (2025-2026) literature: LLM- and foundation-model-based trajectory reasoning for Cluster A; agentic, LLM-driven security-operations copilots for Cluster B, including a reported 6.5x improvement in malicious-alert identification over human analysts in one production deployment; learned and graph-neural-network-based approaches to the classical optimisation and graph-isomorphism problems in Cluster C; and natural-language-to-workflow agentic automation for the low-code and embedded-systems work in Cluster D. Throughout, we explicitly separate what the reviewed papers themselves established from this review's own forward-looking analysis, and close with a discussion of the reliability, interpretability, and adversarial-robustness risks that accompany each proposed direction.

candidates.title: Staged Continual Adaptation of Multimodal Foundation Models for Japanese Financial Documents
candidates.abstract: Staged post-training of multimodal foundation models chains vision-language alignment, reasoning distillation, and domain tuning, yet how each phase trades capabilities against the others remains under-characterised. Tracking an 8.4B-parameter model from an un-fine-tuned baseline through three training phases on Japanese financial documents (evaluated on five text-input benchmarks), we find the phases interact non-additively: math-only distillation overwrites the financial knowledge acquired earlier even as procedural math skill survives, and the domain phase repairs more than it installs. A skip-phase ablation is best for domain knowledge but forfeits numerical-reasoning gains, so per-phase contributions are not decomposable and the best checkpoint is task-dependent, with implications for checkpoint retention and scheduling rather than added stages.

candidates.title: Local Inference of LLMs on Long Contexts: A Data Systems Perspective
candidates.abstract: Large language models can solve complex problems across a variety of subjects, such as mathematics and coding. For such complex analytical tasks, models with a long context perform better. Serving models with long context is currently mostly done on powerful systems with multiple GPUs, which are too expensive for most users. An alternative is local inference, or serving a model on a user's own machine, which removes per-token costs and rate limits, besides keeping sensitive data private and giving users full control over the models they run. The common understanding, however, is that local LLMs need compression (e.g., quantization) to run on a single GPU. In this paper, we set out to study the limitations that prevent serving long-context models for single users, besides the capacity issue. Rather than characterizing a single model on one GPU, we analyze how different models behave across several GPU generations. This lets us uncover not just individual bottlenecks but broader trends in where inefficiencies arise. Our analysis confirms that, as expected, self-attention dominates the runtime for long-context inference. More unexpectedly, our evaluation reveals that the current structure of self-attention leaves key GPU resources significantly underutilized, and the newest GPU is often the least well served. Many of these findings are fundamentally data management problems, from paging the KV cache to improving cache utilization and synchronization in the GPU, which is why we bring this study to the Data Systems community. To engage this community, we present our findings as a series of experimental observations and formulate recommendations for future work.

candidates.title: GBClaw: An agentic AI framework for atomistic grain boundary research and mechanistic discovery
candidates.abstract: Agentic artificial intelligence (AI) systems hold immense potential for automating complex workflows in materials discovery and design, but extending them to domain-intensive mechanistic investigations remains challenging. Here, we present GBClaw, an agentic AI framework for investigating the structure and deformation of general grain boundaries (GBs). Although general GBs constitute the vast majority of real-world interfaces in polycrystalline materials, they remain understudied because their structural complexity and interfacial mismatch complicate experimental and modeling research. GBClaw integrates large language models (LLMs) into a modular architecture comprising an orchestrator, specialized agents, domain-specific tools, simulation interfaces, and hierarchical memory. Through dynamic replanning and iterative workflow refinement, the framework effectively connects systematic simulations with targeted mechanistic analysis. Applied to 14 general asymmetric tilt GBs in nickel, GBClaw characterized interfacial defect structures and identified diverse deformation modes across these incommensurate boundaries. Comparing boundary sliding with and without secondary GB misfit dislocations revealed substantial differences in shear strength, underscoring the critical role of defect hierarchies in sliding resistance. Furthermore, researcher-guided follow-up calculations traced an anomalously high shear resistance to metastable boundary structures. This work demonstrates that combining agentic AI with domain expertise bridges high-throughput computational screening with deep physical understanding of complex material interfaces.

candidates.title: Agentic Ensemble with Vision-Language Models for Visual Anomaly Detection
candidates.abstract: Visual anomaly detection aims to detect abnormal objects, while anomaly samples are often scarce during model training. Assembling multiple pretrained detectors can help by leveraging their transferable image scores and anomaly maps. However, most existing ensemble methods apply fixed fusion rules over saved predictions which struggle when pretrained detectors clearly disagree due to different training objectives, priors, and visual representations. To this end, we design AnomalyAgent, a post-training fusion framework for accurate visual anomaly detection. AnomalyAgent aligns heterogeneous scores and maps, summarizes score- and region-level disagreement, and treats fusion as a finite action-selection problem. It implements two types of actions: 1) score actions that determine how to fuse image-level detector confidence via consensus, robust aggregation, detector weighting, or score-map consistency; 2) map actions that fuse dense anomaly responses via consensus, detector weighting, geometric aggregation, or disagreement correction. A constrained vision-language model (VLM) is introduced to inspect high-conflict samples and select valid score action and map action to produce the final prediction. We evaluate AnomalyAgent on MVTec AD and VisA as primary benchmarks, together with seven additional public anomaly benchmarks and Real-IAD for large-scale score-level evaluation. Across these benchmarks, AnomalyAgent consistently improves over equal-weight fusion and achieves the best mean image AUROC and pixel AP among the compared fusion methods on MVTec AD and VisA, while demonstrating robust transfer across additional anomaly domains.

candidates.title: Why Customers Welcome or Resist AI Salespeople: Formation Mechanisms of Algorithm Aversion and Algorithm Appreciation in Large Language Model Sales
candidates.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) now answer product questions, recommend items and help close deals in online shops, banks and telecom services. Customers react to these AI sales agents in two opposite ways. Some avoid them, a pattern researchers call algorithm aversion, while others prefer them to human advice, a pattern called algorithm appreciation. This paper reviews the main empirical studies on both patterns and asks how each one forms when the "algorithm" is a conversational sales agent. Drawing on research in judgment and decision making, consumer behavior and human computer interaction, it proposes a framework with three layers. The first layer contains the cues that an LLM sales agent gives off. The second layer contains five psychological pathways that operate during the conversation: competence belief, error sensitivity, empathy and uniqueness concern, social presence, and perceived control. The third layer contains situational conditions such as product type, the timing of AI identity disclosure, the customer's emotional state and prior AI experience. Six propositions are derived. The paper argues that aversion and appreciation are not fixed traits of customers but outcomes of how these layers combine in a particular sales encounter, and it discusses implications for firms and for future student research.
candidates.venue: Advances in Economics, Management and Political Sciences

candidates.title: When Can LLM Reasoning Reliably Reuse Intermediate Results?
candidates.abstract: Sampling complete solutions gives large language models more chances to solve a problem, but each attempt starts again. For tasks with several subproblems, all required answers must be correct in the same attempt. Retaining intermediate results can avoid repeating correct work, but errors in those results may affect later attempts. We study when this reuse is reliable and how much computation it requires. For local retries that stop when no candidate passes within the retry budget, we give conditions for correct completion and bound the average number of attempts. We also show how checking cost and the chance of passing a check affect total computation. Experiments across eight reasoning models examine composite mathematics and arithmetic. Across four DeepSeek models, average success on the second subproblem is 36.2 percent without first-subproblem context, 57.2 percent with its answer, and 58.3 percent with its reasoning and answer. These scores measure second-subproblem coverage and include continuations made when selection fails. Arithmetic experiments show that similar first-attempt accuracies can lead to very different coverage after repeated attempts. Code is available at https://github.com/SempraETY/Intermediate-State-Reuse.

candidates.title: Transforming Research Management and Knowledge Creation With Large Language Models
candidates.abstract: Abstract The rapid advancement of Large Language Models (LLMs) has fundamentally transformed academic research and institutional operations. Major LLMs, such as OpenAI’s ChatGPT, Anthropic’s Claude, Google’s Gemini, and Microsoft Copilot, are now integrated into educational institutions at research and administrative levels. These LLMs go beyond summarizing text or polishing emails to include personalized learning, automated content creation, decision-making, and pedagogical integration. This chapter investigates the evolving role of LLMs in transforming the research landscape, particularly in academic writing, research management, pedagogy, evaluation, and ethical consideration. The research method is based on a systematic literature review (SLR) following PRISMA protocols, supported by bibliometric analysis and keyword-based thematic analysis of peer-reviewed articles from Web of Science and Scopus databases (2020–2025). Results revealed the existence of five major themes, namely academic writing and content generation, research evaluation, pedagogical integration, model comparison, and ethical considerations. The study highlights a sharp increase in publications since ChatGPT’s emergence, with thematic shifts toward education-related applications. Heatmaps across Scopus and WoS demonstrated significant trends toward real-world educational applications. However, ethical concerns showed strong growth, reflecting academic integrity issues. The keyword co-occurrence analysis also showed a dynamic research landscape with strong thematic ties to ethics, academic writing, teaching, and educational innovation. The overlay visualizations further illustrated the temporal evolution of topics from foundational concepts toward technology adoption, user experience, and collaborative learning. This chapter concludes by suggesting some recommendations to guide institutional policy and future research, ensuring an effective integration of LLMs in academic settings.

candidates.title: TeCoP: Accelerating Diffusion Large Language Model Decoding via Tentative Context Pipelining
candidates.abstract: Diffusion large language models (dLLMs) predict multiple token positions per forward pass, yet block-wise decoders serialize generation and repeatedly recompute stable predictions. We attribute this inefficiency to coupling a prediction's readiness for irreversible commitment with its utility as context. We introduce Tentative Context Pipelining (TeCoP), a training-free decoder that decouples these roles through staggered block-parallel pipelining and draft-and-verify. TeCoP reuses stable but uncommitted predictions as provisional cross-block context, with commitment governed by confidence and stability checks. Across four LLaDA and Dream dLLMs on GSM8K, Minerva MATH, and MBPP, TeCoP reduces number of forward evaluations by up to 87% and achieves up to 7.50-fold throughput without KV caching and 11.77-fold with caching over the uncached original decoder. It outperforms Fast-dLLM and DSB in throughput across all 12 model-benchmark settings, with and without caching, while keeping average cached accuracy within one percentage point of the original decoder.

candidates.title: Speak vs. Know: Balancing Behavior and Knowledge Distributions of Large Language Models
candidates.abstract: Recent work reports that the distribution verbalized directly in the output text aligns far better with human opinion distributions than the next-token log-probability distribution of LLMs. However, the verbalized distribution reflects what LLMs know about a group's opinions (knowledge distribution), while what they actually output at deployment is governed by their log-probability distribution (behavior distribution). We find that when prompting LLMs to predict the opinion of a specific group, the most likely answer under the verbalized distribution differs from that under the log-probability distribution for 37% of World Values Survey questions, averaged over three LLMs. Thus, LLMs' knowledge does not match their behavior. This matters for evaluation: a verbalized distribution can score well against a group while its most likely answer is one the model never outputs, so the score no longer describes the model. The alignment scores for these two distributions reflect only the model's behavior or its knowledge, separately. We therefore propose a learnable combination of the two distributions that follows the most likely answer of the behavior distribution while preserving the shape of the knowledge distribution, with a single hyperparameter trading off behavioral fidelity against distribution quality. Our experiments on three opinion survey datasets and six models show that the balanced distribution improves behavioral consistency over the verbalized distribution from 71.6% to 95.6% on average, while the total variation distance to the human opinion distributions rises only slightly from 28.8% to 33.8%, and it remains effective under temperature scaling and cross-dataset settings.

candidates.title: Source Page Evaluation of Local RAG Retrieval for Engineering Safety: Implications for Mechanical and Civil Engineering
candidates.abstract: Industrial safety question answering requires access to the exact source material that supports an answer, not merely a related document. This study evaluates the retrieval stage of a local retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) system at the source page level. Eighteen documents on lockout/tagout, machine guarding, and personal protective equipment were prepared in raw, cleaned, and metadata-enriched forms. Best Matching 25 (BM25), latent semantic analysis (LSA), and reciprocal rank fusion (RRF) hybrid retrieval were tested on 54 questions: 36 answerable, 12 safety-related but unsupported, and 6 outside the covered topics. Raw BM25 achieved the highest mean reciprocal rank (0.492) and Hit@5 (0.722), cleaned BM25 achieved the highest Hit@3 (0.556) and answerability AUROC (0.765), and metadata-enriched BM25 achieved the highest Hit@10 (0.833). For raw text, the retrieval method affected reciprocal rank (Friedman χ2 = 7.13, p = 0.028). Hybrid retrieval exceeded LSA after Holm correction (p = 0.011), whereas BM25 and hybrid retrieval did not differ (p = 0.302). Text preparation had no overall effect within BM25 (p = 0.220). The results show that document-level evaluation can overstate access to exact evidence. The study provides a repeatable procedure for source tracking, page-level relevance labeling, separate retrieval and generation evaluation, and refusal analysis. These design principles are also relevant to construction safety knowledge systems that combine regulations, accident reports, project data, and BIM-linked information. Because the relevance set is a model-assisted silver standard, the findings remain exploratory rather than expert-certified absolute retrieval accuracy. A controlled same-run extension with all MiniLM L6 v2 and BM25 + MiniLM RRF is reported separately; its observed fusion gains did not reach statistical significance on the 36 answerable questions. The work is intended to support safety engineers, researchers, and developers designing evidence-grounded industrial and construction safety information systems.

candidates.title: Rewards for Budget-Aware Multi-Turn Agents That Adapt to Arbitrary Test-Time Constraints
candidates.abstract: Large language model agents are often given an inference budget and asked to maximise success within it. A multi-turn agent has to allocate this budget across many environment interactions. An external harness can enforce the budget, but it remains unclear whether the agent itself can learn when and how much to spend. We ask whether agents can learn this allocation across dynamically specified budgets and which rewards best teach this behaviour. We adapt existing length penalties to budget constraints spanning multiple resource types, introduce new reward formulations, and compare eleven objectives in a shared training pipeline. We train Qwen3.5 models at 4B and 9B on AppWorld with budgets over tokens, API calls, and environment steps, and on the BabyAI gridworld with turn budgets. We train a separate policy for each environment and resource type, with each policy trained across budget values. Training with rewards that penalise overspending substantially improves within-budget success and natural compliance over untrained models and over training on task success alone, with agents learning to adapt their resource use to stated budgets and task difficulty. These gains extend to unseen budgets and, zero-shot, to a shifted task distribution and a new benchmark. Reward objectives trade off success within budget and natural compliance. A sigmoid penalty for overspending most often achieves the highest within-budget success at an individual budget, while a fixed negative reward for overspending generally yields the strongest natural compliance. Combining penalties for overspend frequency and magnitude gives the smallest average gap to the best method at each budget. Overall, we show that a single agent can learn to allocate resources across turns and adapt its behaviour to user-specified budgets using budget feedback without external budget-allocation controllers.

candidates.title: PI-MLLM: Psychophysics-Inspired Multimodal Large Language Model for Oddly Satisfying Video Emotion Analysis
candidates.abstract: Oddly Satisfying Videos (OSVs) can evoke strong viewer responses through repetitive motion, visual tactility, and ASMR-like sounds despite containing few explicit semantic emotion cues. This makes OSVs a challenging setting for Video Emotion Analysis (VEA), since most existing methods focus on semantic video content and under-model the physical sensory dynamics that shape viewer responses. To support Oddly Satisfying Video Emotion Analysis (OSVEA), we construct the Oddly Satisfying Video Dataset (OSVD), comprising 12,000 annotated 5-second clips. Each clip provides viewer-emotion labels under video-only, audio-only, and audio-visual conditions, together with explanations grounded in visual and acoustic sensory evidence. Building on OSVD, we propose PI-MLLM, a psychophysics-inspired multimodal large language model that integrates Modality-Specific Dynamics Alignment (MSDA) and Coalition-Based Audio-Visual Attribution (CAVA). MSDA uses auxiliary prediction objectives to align modality representations with visual motion and acoustic energy-onset dynamics. CAVA evaluates emotion scores across modality coalitions and applies Shapley attribution to identify the dominant modality and determine whether visual and auditory evidence is synergistic or conflicting. Experiments show that PI-MLLM improves both viewer-side emotion prediction and sensory-grounded explanation quality, suggesting the value of physical sensory cues to video emotion analysis.

candidates.title: Learned Readout Tokens for Extracting Large Language Model Confidence
candidates.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used within everyday applications where their responses have significant downstream impacts. For responsible deployment of such systems, we desire insight into how much we can trust their individual outputs. A popular approach for estimating LLM confidence is to train probes on the hidden states of the LLM's tokens to predict the correctness of the model's output. These probes typically read hidden states from tokens that are already in the model's vocabulary. In this work, we introduce a new approach to confidence probes that learn a new readout token and utilize its hidden states to train the probe. We show that our learned readout approach ScratchProbe outperforms its existing-token counterpart on a variety of datasets and LLMs. We also extend our method to a multi-token approach which we show provides further performance improvements. Finally, since the learned readout changes only the position a probe reads from, any existing probe can adopt it. Applied to a state-of-the-art probe, it improves AUROC on every backbone, in domain and out of domain.

candidates.title: Hallucinations of Large Language Models in Cross-Language Code Translation: Phenomena and Mitigation
candidates.abstract: Code translation converts source code from one programming language to another while preserving its functionality. Although Large Language Models (LLMs) have improved code translation, their outputs still contain hallucinations: generated code that conflicts with the source program, violates target-language facts, or introduces contextually inconsistent dependencies. These failures are especially harmful in translation because small semantic deviations can silently change program behavior. Existing hallucination studies mainly focus on natural-language generation or code generation, leaving the forms, distribution, and mitigation of hallucinations in cross-language code translation insufficiently characterized. This paper presents a systematic empirical study of LLM hallucinations in code translation. Across three benchmark datasets, six language pairs, and seven LLMs, we construct a taxonomy with three major categories: Semantic Consistency Conflicts, Factual Knowledge Conflicts, and Project Context Deviations. We manually annotate 13,919 hallucination cases and analyze how hallucination types vary across models, datasets, and language directions. Guided by the taxonomy, we further propose HaluCodeTran, a mitigation framework that combines BM25-based retrieval of relevant translation examples with taxonomy-aware reflective refinement. The study provides an execution-tested characterization of code-translation hallucinations and a practical baseline for building more reliable LLM-based code migration tools.

candidates.title: From Ethical Principles to Governable Action: A Priority Architecture for Context-Sensitive Normative Governance of Large Language Models
candidates.abstract: Abstract Responsible artificial intelligence frameworks converge around principles including non-maleficence, beneficence, autonomy, justice, privacy, responsibility, and explicability, but they do not determine action when principles conflict or specify how contextual priorities should be enforced. This paper introduces the Priority Architecture (PA), a metamodel for context-sensitive normative governance of large language models (LLMs). PA represents a traceable refinement chain from a disclosed normative foundation through Context Dimensions, Priority Patterns, and Resolution Modes to Action Envelopes and enforcement, while externalizing priority resolution from the model. A proof of concept instantiates PA for an enterprise-internal LLM assistant handling synthetic private contact data and replicates a fixed protocol with GPT-5.6 Sol and Claude Sonnet 5. GPT-5.6-Sol-based coding classified 100/120 baseline responses and 120/120 responses under strong policy prompting and external PA governance as compliant for GPT; for Claude the counts were 92/120, 108/120, and 120/120. The prompt-versus-PA difference was confined to two difficult case types and was measurement-sensitive. The 1,440-response coding was evaluated on a stratified 20\% human sample. Two independent human coders agreed on 281/288 items (97.6\%); among these consensus items, GPT-5.6 Sol agreed on 275/281 (97.9\%). No extraction errors occurred in the benchmark, but ambiguous or adversarial inputs were not tested. The results support the narrower claim that normative priority resolution can be externalized into an explicit, deterministic, machine-readable, and auditable governance object; they establish neither model independence nor inherent ethical superiority.

candidates.title: From Encoding to Generation: Towards Empathetic Large Language Models
candidates.abstract: Empathetic interaction involves two distinguishable capacities: representing another person's emotional state (cognitive empathy) and generating an appropriate response to that state (affective empathy). We apply this distinction to examine how emotion-related information is internally organized, selectively attended to, and carried through response generation in Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct across 10 emotion categories from the EmpatheticDialogues dataset. Layer-wise linear probing revealed a broad middle-layer region of peak emotion-category decodability, with the layer-11 L2 probe achieving 63.6% held-out accuracy against a 10% chance level and a 54.6% TF-IDF lexical baseline. During response generation, emotion-related user tokens received 1.89 times as much attention per token as other utterance tokens, concentrated across layers 10-15. Target-emotion alignment then decreased from a mean cosine similarity of 0.239 for input representations to 0.125 for generated responses, with positive drift in 77% of examples and the largest shifts for angry and furious. Emotion-category representation, attention allocation, and response-level alignment therefore emerge as distinguishable components of model processing that can be analyzed through a functional cognitive-affective empathy framework. These findings provide a foundation for monitoring emotion representations during generation and leveraging models' existing affective structure to support more naturally empathetic responses without relying on external prompting or explicit emotion conditioning.

candidates.title: Detecting Errors in Large Language Model Responses: The Incremental Predictive Value of Hidden States
candidates.abstract: Although large language models support a wide range of tasks, hallucinations remain a major obstacle to user trust. When a model generates an answer, both its internal processing and final output vary with the question. Internal states are often expected to offer richer signals for hallucination detection. However, studies using these states typically report their standalone discrimination performance, while output-side comparisons often use simple baselines with weaker modeling capacity. We integrate output-side information available at inference time into a combined baseline and compare detection performance before and after adding hidden states under identical data splits and evaluation rules. Experiments cover open-ended generation and constrained multiple-choice tasks across different models. Adding hidden states improves AUROC by approximately 0.004 and 0.039 on the two tasks, respectively. Hidden states thus provide additional predictive information, but strong standalone detection performance can still yield only limited additional gains.

candidates.title: DeclineCraft: A RAG Abstention Benchmark for Jointly Measuring Combined Retrieval and Parametric Knowledge
candidates.abstract: Reliable retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) requires recognizing when neither retrieved documents nor parametric knowledge supports an answer. We introduce DeclineCraft, a dynamic abstention benchmark whose unanswerable questions target Minecraft feature additions after a corpus cut-off, with audits of possible parametric exposure. Later cut-offs support evaluation of future models. Across 27 LLMs, we measure Correct Abstention Rate (CAR; how often models acknowledge insufficient knowledge on unanswerable questions), Answerable Attempt Rate and Answer Accuracy. We find that (1) single-shot retrieval significantly raises CAR in 38 of 40 configurations (model and thinking setting) versus no retrieval. (2) Iterative RAG, in which the model self-assesses its context and can request up to two further retrieval rounds, significantly lowers CAR versus single-shot RAG in 30 of 40 configurations (mean 46.4%), with little change in Answer Accuracy (68.5% to 69.3%). Adding query rewriting and reranking to hybrid (dense & sparse) retrieval lowers CAR for all 12 models tested. (3) Larger models answer more accurately (Spearman $ρ= +0.60$ with total parameters), but neither model size nor release date shows a significant association with CAR. (4) Without retrieval, enabling thinking on the same weights lowers CAR significantly for 8 of 13 models (by 14% points on average), and the responses shift from acknowledged uncertainty to premise denial.

candidates.title: Context-Aware Prompt Injection Detection via Small Language Models in RAG Pipelines: nokast-secureRAG
candidates.abstract: Local Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems are vulnerable to indirect prompt injection and retrieval poisoning, where malicious instructions in retrieved content are mistaken for trusted input. We present nokast-secureRAG, a roughly 0.5B-parameter small language model that acts as a semantic firewall between retrieval and generation. It jointly evaluates the user query and retrieved context, classifying the pair as safe, suspicious, or malicious. The model is trained using a teacher-judge-student pipeline: a 35B teacher generates 5,233 examples across four attack families, and an independent 120B judge re-labels them, achieving 95.0% agreement before student fine-tuning. On a held-out in-distribution test set, the model achieves 0.994 detection recall at a 0.026 false-positive rate and a 0.006 attack-success-rate proxy, outperforming a regex baseline, a public prompt-injection classifier, Llama Guard 3 1B, and its untuned version. Prompt-Guard-86M reaches 0.900 recall but has a 0.690 false-positive rate. On a judgment-flip test, where the same sentence is benign or malicious depending on context, the model correctly classifies both cases 75% of the time, outperforming the compared baselines. Ablations indicate that retrieved context carries the main attack signal, while query-context consistency reduces false positives. Single-request latency is 293-404 ms, above the target of 100 ms, while amortized throughput latency is 37 ms under batching. On the external PoisonedRAG benchmark, recall falls to near zero, indicating that fluent fact-poisoning attacks lie outside the detector's instruction-consistency threat model. We report this limitation alongside the in-distribution results. The model, data-generation pipeline, and evaluation harness are released open source.

candidates.title: Building Telecom Language Models with RSOD: Domain Data, Specialist Post-Training, Memory-Conscious Distillation, and Networking Evaluation
candidates.abstract: Telecom language models must combine broad networking knowledge with specialist behavior across routing, broadband services, access technologies, and operational diagnostics while remaining practical to deploy as a single model. We present an end-to-end framework that builds source-grounded synthetic training data from structured networking taxonomies and expert graphs, materializes 212,559 routed training records across fourteen networking routes, trains six frozen specialist LoRA teachers over one shared continued-pretrained backbone, and consolidates their behavior into one deployable student adapter using Routed Specialist On-Policy Distillation (RSOD). In RSOD, the committed student generates each trajectory, the route-assigned specialist teacher-forces the exact native token sequence, compact teacher hidden states are reconstructed through the shared frozen output head, and only the student LoRA is updated. A controlled reconstruction validation shows mean absolute logit error of 7.26 x 10^-6 with 100% top-1 agreement between native and reconstructed teacher logits. On four RTX 6000 Ada GPUs, the completed 2,000-step run produced 16,000 trajectories with zero observed student-version or token- ID mismatches. Under the primary route-conditioned evaluation over 2,850 held-out questions, the raw Meta-Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model scores 12.8661/25 micro (13.0172/25 macro), the combined routed six-teacher system scores 21.7641/25 micro, and the consolidated RSOD student, released as Llama-CalixCLM v1, reaches 21.7112/25 micro (21.8006/25 macro) on the same five dimension LLM-judge rubric. Under a separate neutral deployment-like prompt, the same student reaches 20.0028/25 micro (20.0778/25 macro). The consolidated student remains within 0.0529 micro-score points of the combined routed-teacher system while retaining a numerically validated and auditable train-serve execution path.

candidates.title: BitMTP: When Multi-Token Prediction Meets Low-Bit Large Language Models
candidates.abstract: For efficient deployment of large language models (LLMs), methods of ultra-low-bit backbones reduce weight storage, memory traffic, and linear-layer execution cost, while multi-token prediction (MTP) methods reduce sequential decoding steps by predicting multiple future tokens in parallel. Although complementary, the direct combination of these methods cannot accelerate decoding at comparable quality: masked drafting lacks intermediate token input supplied in next-token training, while wider computation and causal key-value (KV) updates can offset the savings from fewer steps. To address these challenges, we propose BitMTP, an algorithm-system co-design framework for efficient MTP on ultra-low-bit LLM backbones. A joint next-token prediction and MTP objective equips a single model with both autoregressive (AR) generation and block-causal drafting. Confidence-only decoding, speculative-only decoding, and hybrid decoding provide different quality-throughput operating points without using separate draft and verifier models. Accepted-prefix alignment keeps the committed prefix, materialized causal KV boundary, and CUDA Graph replay state consistent for continued generation. BitMTP uses this contract to select width-specialized low-bit execution and reuse captured graphs over shared KV storage. On NVIDIA H20, BitMTP with hybrid decoding achieves five-task mean speedups of 2.2x on BitNet b1.58-2B and 2.1-2.4x on 1.7B-4B Bonsai models at comparable task quality. On RTX 3090 and Jetson Orin, it further achieves up to 2.0x in five-task mean throughput and 3.3x on MBPP+, respectively. These results demonstrate that BitMTP accelerates ultra-low-bit LLM generation across backbones, model sizes, and GPU types. The source code is released at https://github.com/PolyU-VCLab/BitMTP

candidates.title: Beyond 4 bits: Data-Centric Post-training Quantization and Recovery
candidates.abstract: Post-training quantization (PTQ) compresses the weights of a trained model with limited compute and data. Down to 4 bits it is near-lossless, but at 2 bits scalar PTQ configurations fall to chance-level accuracy. We study three choices usually treated as implementation details that matter little at 4 bits but decide 2-bit quality: the quantization representation, the calibration data, and the recovery fine-tuning data, across six dense and mixture-of experts models (ranging from $3.8$ to $32$B parameters). Representation is the largest factor and vector codebooks restore usable models where scalar PTQ pipelines collapse. Most of the remaining loss in accuracy is on \emph{generative} tasks, and the amount of performance drop is model-dependent. Furthermore, at a short recovery budget, calibration and recovery data are coupled. The best recovery data depends on the calibration data, so the two must be chosen jointly. The resulting recipe involves a vector codebook representation, a small task-aligned calibration mixture, and an inexpensive codebook-only recovery stage. Including codebooks, it uses about $2.3$ effective bits per weight and retains $89$ to $97\%$ of full-precision question-answering (QA) accuracy where scalar PTQ is at chance, and, including recovery, uses $1.4$ to $30\times$ less compute than the strongest quantization-aware-training (QAT) baseline.

candidates.title: ACE-Compression: An Ability-Centric Evaluation of Compressed Large Language Models
candidates.abstract: Model compression makes large language models deployable, but today's evaluation tells an incomplete story. Standard practice measures retained task performance and stops there. This misses a critical fact: compression perturbs the distributed knowledge embedded across billions of weights, and task scores alone cannot reveal which underlying abilities survive and which quietly collapse. To solve this question, we introduce ACE-Compression, an ability-centric evaluation framework. Instead of asking only "does the compressed model still answer correctly?", we ask "which of its core abilities remain intact?" Our framework probes four deployment-facing dimensions: procedural reasoning and constraint execution, knowledge grounding and truthfulness, social cognition and affective understanding, and persona fidelity and stylistic consistency. Across more than 35 compressed checkpoints from six open-weight LLMs-covering quantization and pruning-we find that compression redistributes ability profiles. Coarse, local, and surface-level signals often persist, while fine-grained, long-tail, and context-dependent abilities become fragile. Quantization consistently outperforms pruning in retention, but the practical meaning of that gap depends entirely on which ability an application requires. Based on our findings, deployers can choose compression methods by the ability profile their application needs, not just by a leaderboard average. And algorithm designers gain diagnostic signals to build compression methods that preserve what matters. We believe that ACE-Compression turns compression from a black-box accuracy drop into an interpretable intervention-one we can measure, understand, and ultimately improve.

candidates.title: ABench: Adversarily Benchmarking Large Language Models across Taxonomized Values
candidates.abstract: Ensuring the alignment of Large Language Models (LLMs) with diverse cultural values is critical for their safe global deployment. However, existing alignment benchmarks are predominantly English-centric or confined to simple discriminative tasks. Moreover, they often fail to effectively evaluate model robustness against complex, adversarial inductions within specific cultural contexts. To address these limitations, we propose ABench, a fine-grained, handcrafted benchmark specifically tailored to taxonomized values in Chinese. Grounded in a rigorous hierarchical taxonomy comprising 158 derived value subcategories, ABench consists of 2,895 open-ended questions. These questions employ techniques such as role-playing and logical traps to probe the stability of models' stances in adversarially induced contexts. Furthermore, we propose a weighted automated evaluation framework that utilizes question-specific scoring criteria for nuanced assessment. Extensive experiments on 16 mainstream LLMs reveal that most models exhibit significant vulnerabilities when subjected to sophisticated adversary attacks on values (scoring below 60). This underscores the need for more robust, culturally specific alignment strategies. Our data will be publicly released to promote further research on taxonomized value alignment.

candidates.title: A Unified Attack Framework against Statistical Generative Watermarks for Large Language Models
candidates.abstract: Watermarking has emerged as a key tool for identifying text generated by large language models (LLMs), with current schemes embedding statistical signals into the generation process to enable later detection. In this work, we identify a shared weakness across a broad class of popular LLM watermarking methods, including KGW (and its variants), GumbelSoft, DipMark, ITS, and SynthID. We show that these schemes exhibit a fundamental link between their detection scores and the token probability shifts they introduce during generation. This link, which we call score-ratio alignment, allows an attacker with only black-box query access to the model--and no knowledge of secret keys or model weights--to produce text that evades detection while remaining fluent and natural. We prove that the resulting attack is optimal across all covered watermark families, and show that the weakness is intrinsic: any watermark designed to maximize statistical detection power necessarily induces the very structure that attackers can exploit. We evaluate our attack on seven popular generative LLM watermarking schemes, three LLMs, and tasks, which reduce detection rates to at most 0.05 across all settings while preserving text quality. Our findings show that current watermarking methods can be reliably defeated under realistic attack conditions, highlighting the need for fundamentally different watermarking designs that decouple detection scores from token probability shifts.

candidates.title: VGL-stGen: Learning a shared multimodal model for lung histology and spatial transcriptomics

Training integrates image-expression and expression-cell-type pairs, and gene-conditioned pseudo-labels transfer transcriptomic cell-type supervision to histology images. One deployed checkpoint supports thirteen evaluated tasks spanning tissue and cell-type classification, gene prediction and conditional expression completion from combinations of histology, cell identity and observed gene expression. Task-specific decoding produces categorical labels, gene lists and structured expression levels. For conditional completion, fixing queried gene identities and predicting their levels autoregressively improves structured prediction. Controlled adaptation shows that restricting supervision to requested expression-level tokens can further improve image-conditioned completion. Image-permutation experiments indicate that correctly paired histology adds information beyond observed expression. External classification relies partly on computational references with shared annotation lineage, and some H&E sources were exposed during cancer training or model development. Within these conditions, VGL-stGen demonstrates how a medical vision-language backbone can learn from spatial transcriptomics and histology to connect tissue morphology and molecular states through shared generative modeling.

candidates.title: Temporal Evidence-Parameter Co-Alignment for LLM Reasoning over Temporal Knowledge Graphs
candidates.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) often struggle with temporally grounded reasoning because their static parametric memory is misaligned with the dynamic evolution of real-world knowledge. Although RAG and Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT) provide practical ways to enhance LLMs, they remain insufficient for temporal reasoning. Existing retrieval methods typically prioritize semantic relevance while overlooking temporal validity, event order, and evolutionary dependencies, resulting in evidence that is relevant in isolation but temporally fragmented. Meanwhile, conventional PEFT methods usually employ fixed and input-agnostic low-rank updates, making it difficult to capture time-dependent entity semantics and relation drift. To address these limitations, we propose Temporal Evidence-Parameter Co-Alignment (TEPCA), a framework for LLM reasoning over TKGs. TEPCA aligns LLM reasoning with temporal knowledge at both the evidence and parameter levels. At the evidence level, it introduces time-constrained Dynamic Relevance-Guided Path (DRGP) pruning to preserve globally coherent temporal paths, together with Mutual-Information (MI)-based pruning to retain query-informative local facts under temporal constraints. At the parameter level, it integrates Dynamic-Gated LoRA (DG-LoRA), a timestamp-conditioned low-rank adaptation mechanism that dynamically modulates the effective adaptation subspace according to temporal context. This design enables LLMs to better capture fine-grained entity evolution and time-dependent relation semantics while preserving parameter efficiency. Experimental results on two TKG benchmarks demonstrate that TEPCA achieves state-of-the-art performance. Additional evaluations of DG-LoRA on eight commonsense QA datasets further verify its general input-adaptive capacity, scalability across LLM backbones, and interpretability.

candidates.title: Stratified Sparse Attention: Reducing the Sparse-to-Dense Gap at Extreme Sparsity
candidates.abstract: Large Language Model inference over long contexts is increasingly bottlenecked by the cost of attending to a growing Key-Value (KV) cache. Sparse attention reduces this cost by accessing only a fraction of the cache, but existing methods face a trade-off between deterministic retrieval, which captures high-scoring tokens but discards residual attention mass, and sampling, which improves coverage at the cost of higher variance. Hybrid methods combine top-$k$ retrieval with uniform sampling, yet still exhibit a substantial gap from dense attention at aggressive sparsity. We introduce \emph{Stratified Sparse Attention (SSA)}, a unified framework combining deterministic retrieval with score-guided sampling. SSA deterministically attends to high-scoring tokens while sampling the residual using proxy attention scores and correcting for their inclusion probabilities, thereby recovering attention mass beyond the retrieval set. SSA encompasses top-$k$, top-$p$, and hybrid top-$k$+sampling as special cases. Across RULER, LongBench, LOFT, and AIME, and five models ranging from 3B to 27B parameters, SSA consistently improves over the baselines at matched sparsity. candidates.title: RACE: RoPE-Aligned Attention Compression Based on Query-Key Activation Energies
candidates.abstract: Head-dimension compression can reduce the memory required by the key-value (KV) cache, but existing methods often reconstruct full-dimensional representations during inference, adding significant decoding FLOPs overhead. We formalize the design considerations for converting pretrained attention into a natively reduced-dimensional form that reduces both KV-cache storage and attention computation using a calibration set. Specifically, we consider reductions that (1) apply a shared projection to queries and keys so that they remain in a common reduced feature space, (2) derive this projection jointly from query and key activations to better preserve their interaction, and (3) are compatible with the pretrained RoPE transformation. To obtain a reconstruction-free realization of this reduction, we restrict it to coordinate selection and theoretically show that RoPE compatibility then holds if and only if complete rotary pairs are retained. Building on this characterization, we introduce RACE, a post-training method that selects rotary pairs using their joint query-key activation energy. We theoretically show that this criterion minimizes a separable, calibration-dependent upper bound on post-RoPE query-key product approximation error. The resulting reductions are folded into the model weights and require neither runtime reconstruction nor specialized kernels. Across three model families and different compression levels, RACE outperforms structured pruning and remains competitive with reconstruction-based methods on language-modeling, zero-shot, and long-context tasks. At 50% KV-cache retention and 256K context, RACE reduces total inference FLOPs by 47.8%, yielding 1.79x higher throughput, 43.2% lower time-to-first-token (TTFT), and 28.1% lower allocated GPU memory in comparison to an uncompressed model.

candidates.title: Projected Distillation: On Learning to Solve Hard Problems from Close, Correct Targets
candidates.abstract: On-policy learning is central to post-training: training on a model's own generations limits distribution shift and helps preserve existing capabilities. On hard problems, however, on-policy RL provides no reward-based learning signal when all attempts fail. On-policy distillation provides next-token supervision from a teacher, but on hard problems, if a rollout goes wrong early, subsequent supervision is conditioned on prefixes that already contain the mistake. Correct behavior can instead come from a gold or teacher solution, but such off-policy targets can differ substantially from the model's generations and, as we show, may erode existing capabilities. We therefore treat on-policyness as a continuum and propose projected distillation, which minimally edits the student's failed attempts into correct targets. The method uses contrastive updates to favor corrections over failed attempts and refreshes these corrections as the student evolves, enabling near-on-policy learning even when all student attempts fail. Theoretically, we prove that the student's learning regret grows with the edit size: it scales linearly with the horizon under minimal correction, as in DAgger, and quadratically under full-answer replacement, as in behavior cloning. Empirically, across two students (Qwen3-8B and OLMo-2-7B) and five domains spanning math, code, science, and tool use, projected distillation gives the highest area under the specialization-retention frontier (best on 8 of 9 cells against GRPO and OPD, and 7 of 9 against SPOT and SODA). Our ablations highlight the importance of online corrections, the contrastive loss, and on-policyness: moving targets farther off-policy steadily worsens the specialization-retention trade-off, with retention falling from 0.916 to 0.744 when minimal corrections are replaced by student-agnostic gold solutions.

candidates.title: MAS-Guard: Unified Guardrails from Individual Agents to Multi-Agent LLM Systems
candidates.abstract: Agentic AI extends large language models (LLMs) from generating responses to planning and executing complex workflows, substantially expanding their utility while exposing applications to unsafe actions, information leakage, and adversarial manipulation. Multi-agent systems further expand these capabilities through specialization and collaboration, but distributed authority, heterogeneous roles, and opaque or potentially compromised participants make safeguarding even more challenging. Existing defenses address important individual threats but provide fragmented coverage across local execution, system-level interactions, and enforcement mechanisms. We introduce MAS-Guard, a unified framework that closes this gap for safeguarding single- and multi-agent AI applications containing both instrumentable and opaque agents. Within instrumentable agents, the proposed local Agent Guardrail (A-Guard) layer applies task-specific experts to assess agentic events. At the system level, developer-owned Agent Charters and a Control Plane combine deterministic structural checks of routes, agent capabilities, and message formats with semantic assessments of roles and message content. These complementary layers enable enforcement through a shared set of interventions: allow, reflection, confirmation, and block. Evaluated across six benchmarks covering diverse single- and multi-agent scenarios with three agent LLMs from different providers, MAS-Guard reduces the overall attack success rate by 71.5-86.3% relative to unguarded agents, while meeting the utility reference criterion on benign tasks.

candidates.title: Elicitation or Expansion? Demystifying Gains from Agent Harness Optimization
candidates.abstract: Recent studies in harness optimization have shown substantial performance gains in language model agents without updating model weights. A well-designed harness more effectively leverages the underlying model's capabilities by shaping context, tool use, and execution workflows. However, naïve success rates alone do not fully characterize whether optimized harness yields more reliable success on tasks already within reach (elicitation) or a broader range of solvable tasks (expansion). This distinction is crucial for recursive self-improvement and evolutionary search, as expansion may provide a broader range of successful experiences to push the capability boundaries. Despite the growing significance, this distinction remains underexplored in harness optimization. We conduct a systematic analysis to study the effect of gains from harness optimization. Building on pass@k analyses in the reinforcement learning (RL) literature that compare models before and after RL training, we compare optimized harnesses with their pre-optimization counterparts. Specifically, we assess changes in reachable task coverage, compare harness optimization with model scaling and increased inference-time compute, and examine how gains vary with task difficulty. Across static prediction and dynamic tasks, we find that pass@1 advantages of harness over stronger interventions can reverse at larger attempt budgets and aggregate gains conceal shortfalls on hard tasks, underscoring the need for a fine-grained diagnosis.

candidates.title: Africa-Papers: A 10-Billion-Token Multi-Domain Academic Corpus for African Foundation Language Models
candidates.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) depend fundamentally on the diversity, depth, and factual rigor of their pre-training corpora. However, contemporary foundational pre-training datasets (such as The Pile, S2ORC, and Dolma) exhibit a severe structural omission: African scientific, medical, legal, and agricultural scholarship constitutes less than 0.5% of global pre-training tokens. Consequently, state-of-the-art models suffer from systematic failure modes when reasoning about tropical epidemiology, localized smallholder agro-ecologies, regional economic governance, and indigenous linguistic structures. To resolve this representation deficit and advance African intellectual sovereignty in artificial intelligence, we introduce Africa-Papers, the largest curated multi-domain Pan-African academic pre-training corpus to date. Comprising over 844,807 full-text papers spanning 10.15 billion tokens across 879 Parquet shards, Africa-Papers unifies four primary scientific streams: (1) continental peer-reviewed journals indexed in DOAJ across 31 African nations, (2) the CGIAR CGSpace agricultural repository, (3) African-authored and African-focused STEM/AI preprints on arXiv, and (4) open-access international publications by scholars affiliated with African institutions indexed via OpenAlex. The entire corpus is processed into layout-aware, clean Markdown preserving section hierarchies, mathematical equations, and tabular data, accompanied by exact BPE token counts and a standardized 8-domain taxonomy. We release Africa-Papers openly on the Hugging Face Hub under the AfriSpeech organization to accelerate continual pre-training and domain evaluation for foundation models globally.

candidates.title: GARRET: Generative Feedback for Region Retrieval in Visual Documents
candidates.abstract: Multimodal retrieval-augmented generation over visually rich documents requires evidence at a finer granularity than entire pages. Existing visual retrievers typically index or return full pages, whereas training region-level retrievers often requires costly query-to-region annotations or noisy model-generated labels. We introduce GARRET, a region-retrieval framework trained from (page, question, answer) triplets through differentiable generative feedback. A shared context-preserving retriever produces page and region multi-vector representations. During training, their retrieval scores define a soft routing distribution over candidate region crops. An auxiliary vision-language model attends to each crop separately, aggregates crop-specific contexts using the routing weights, and predicts the question followed by the answer under a next-token prediction objective. Gradients through the routing distribution assign query-conditioned credit to the indexed region representations, without requiring query-to-region annotations. At inference, the auxiliary model is removed. GARRET also reuses the contextualized region representations, together with page summary tokens, to construct a compact page representation. We introduce ViDoRe-V3-Region, a corpus-wide benchmark containing 200,682 fixed candidate regions across eight domains. GARRET achieves a macro nDCG@10 of 0.4126, outperforming the strongest visual baseline by 2.94 points. candidates.title: From Scorecards to Agents: A Survey of Anti-Fraud Models Across the Model-Risk Boundary, with a Focus on Evidence Traceability
candidates.abstract: The revised United States guidance on model risk management, issued in April 2026, applies its principles to traditional statistical and quantitative models and to non-generative, non-agentic AI models, and places generative and agentic AI explicitly outside its scope. This survey follows the models used against fraud and financial crime across that line, from rules, scorecards, and statistical tests, through non-generative machine learning, to generative models and language-model agents, across six fraud types. Unlike prior surveys, we place all three generations in one decision-theoretic frame: we restate in one notation known results on cost-optimal and capacity-constrained alerting, undersampling calibration, and the identifiability of recall from alert feedback, express each generation's model, explanation, and validation quantity in that frame, and add two stylized models, one showing why mean aggregation dilutes the neighborhood signal of camouflaged fraudsters and one showing how verifier independence bounds the residual errors in a generated narrative. We find that statistical models and non-generative machine learning have mature validation practice anchored in supervisory guidance, that generative AI now appears both as a tool of fraudsters and as a component of defenses, and that in hybrid pipelines the generative component can write what an analyst or examiner reads although no dedicated supervisory framework covers it. We therefore formalize the evidence-traceability controls that can supply this missing validation as a division of verification labor, between the drafting agent, a deterministic field check, an independent verifier and the human examiner, governed by three parameters an institution can estimate; we then compare the generations quantity by quantity and close with a research agenda.

candidates.title: Why Static Probes Fail: Context Determines Deception Feature Composition
candidates.abstract: With increasing autonomy, Large Language Models (LLMs) may engage in deceptive behaviors, such as scheming to pursue misaligned goals or sandbagging to escape oversight. Monitoring outputs alone is insufficient, as models can produce seemingly benign responses while harboring misaligned internal objectives. While mechanistic approaches like linear probing are promising, they rely on the assumption that deception corresponds to a single direction in representation space. We demonstrate that such single-direction probes fail to generalize across diverse deception scenarios. To bridge this gap, we propose representing deception as a multi-dimensional subspace rather than a single direction. Our method utilizes iterative orthogonal decomposition to identify complementary directions that capture distinct facets of deceptive intent. To effectively leverage these directions for detection, we find that static combinations prove brittle due to strong domain dependence across different scenarios. We therefore introduce a domain-adaptive gating mechanism that dynamically composes the extracted directions through few-shot adaptation at test time. With only 10 examples, our approach achieves an average AUROC of 0.97 and 94% recall at 5% FPR across all evaluated datasets, substantially outperforming existing methods.

candidates.title: Why Do LLMs Accept Generics? Explaining Acceptability using Psycholinguistic and Model-Derived Factors
candidates.abstract: Psycholinguistic studies explore why humans accept some generic statements but reject others by showing that these judgments depend on more than how common a property is.
